conflicts.source_says: ASB 2012 Table 4.10 reports North Gas/Baiji as already transporting 1,270,499 (1,000 scm/yr) of gas in 2011, implying the line was operational before the backend's 2012 construction year.

Al-Ahdab is a CRUDE OIL field, not a gas field. Iraq Business News: 'Reserves: 1 billion barrels of oil. The field also holds 750 billion scf of associated gas reserves, however no plans have been announced for their commercial development, in which case the gas would likely be flared or reinjected.' BBC Arabic headline: 'بدء الانتاج من حقل الاحدب للنفط' ('start of production from the Ahdab OIL field'), 60,000 bbl/day crude, most exported with some used as fuel for nearby power plants. This corroborates the prior-work flag that P4067 is wrong-tracker (crude oil, likely GOIT) -- a gas pipeline carrying Al-Ahdab gas to Al-Zubaydia power station is inconsistent with the field's undeveloped/flared associated gas. No gas-classification refs staged.

The al-mirbad article is about the 'أنبوب تصدير زيت الغاز (شعيبة - ميناء خور الزبير)' -- a GAS OIL / diesel (zeit al-ghaz, a refined petroleum PRODUCT) EXPORT pipeline from the Shuaiba pumping station to Khor Al-Zubair port, not a natural-gas pipeline. Iraq's Oil Pipelines Company (شركة خطوط الأنابيب النفطية) announced completing rehabilitation of the 8-10 inch, 46-km gas-oil export line 'to increase the export capacity of gas-oil fuel via the southern outlet.' This corroborates the prior-work flag that P6824 is wrong-tracker (petroleum products / gas oil, likely GOIT, NOT gas). No gas-classification refs staged. Note the mismatch vs backend length: source says 46 km (backend length was not in scope for this packet).
